description_en: Oracular temple in RugāThe temple is situated on the eastern end of the village of Rugā. The village itslef is located 2 kilometres north of Gamagaḍhī, on the northern bank of the Mugu Karnali river, an important tributary of the Karnali river.The northwest-southeast orientation of the temple follows that of the hill slope along which it is built.Thesanctumoccupies a large rectangular room in the north-west. It is accessed through a little wooden door in the southeastern wall. The other part of the monument consists in a rectangular space with an arcade running on the southwestern and southeastern sides. At the centre of the space is a hearth (kuṇḍa). The wooden pillars that rythm the arcade are richly ornamented with carvings of floral, animal and geometric motifs.The temple is frequented on specific occasions, during which mediums (dhāmī) are possessed by local deities. While the Karnali's oracular practices could be traced from at least the 14th-15th century (Andolfatto 2019: 201-254), the antiquity of the Rugā Maṣṭā Temple is difficult to establish as it was most probably rebuilt over time. Some of the carved wooden elements may be up to 200 years old.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
